title: Tomato and Mozzarella Pasta Salad
subtitle: Short pasta with cherry tomatoes, fresh mozzarella and basil
excerpt: Pasta tossed with halved cherry tomatoes, torn mozzarella and fresh basil, dressed simply with olive oil and balsamic vinegar. A caprese salad in pasta form, best made in summer when tomatoes have some flavour.
sourceNotes: Caprese salad (mozzarella, tomato, basil, olive oil) is a Campanian classic. The pasta version is a British and American adaptation that became popular in the 1990s as mozzarella became widely available. It follows the same flavour logic as the original: ripe summer tomatoes, fresh mozzarella and basil need little else.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook the pasta up to 2 hours ahead; dress and add tomatoes and mozzarella just before serving.

content.text: Tomato and mozzarella pasta salad is a caprese in a bowl, eaten with a fork rather than a knife. It depends entirely on the quality of the tomatoes and mozzarella. Use cherry tomatoes with some sweetness and fresh mozzarella in whey (not the long-life blocks in brine), and it will be good. Add the mozzarella at the last moment so it does not turn rubbery.

Cook {{pasta-dried}} of pasta in well-salted boiling water until just tender. Drain and toss immediately with 1 tablespoon of the olive oil to prevent sticking. Spread on a tray and leave to cool to room temperature, about 10 minutes.

Tip the cooled pasta into a large bowl. Add the cherry tomatoes. Whisk together the remaining {{olive-oil}} of olive oil, {{balsamic-vinegar}} of balsamic vinegar, {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt and {{black-pepper}} of pepper. Pour over the pasta and toss. Add the torn mozzarella and basil and toss once more gently. Serve immediately.

items.cause: Added to warm pasta or dressed too long in advance.
items.fix: Tear and add the mozzarella only just before serving; warm pasta firms it up and makes it chewy.

items.cause: Not tossed with oil immediately after draining.
items.fix: Toss with a small amount of olive oil as soon as it comes out of the colander. Spread the pasta out to cool rather than leaving it in the bowl.

content.text: Tomato and mozzarella pasta salad is a caprese made into a fork dish. It came to British pasta salads in the 1990s as fresh mozzarella and balsamic moved into everyday cooking. Made with good August tomatoes and fresh mozzarella, it is one of the best summer lunches. Made in January with pale tomatoes, it is not worth making.
